text: The Ministry of Power is an Indian government ministry responsible for overseeing electricity production and infrastructure development, including generation, transmission, delivery, and maintenance projects. It serves as a liaison between the central government and state electricity operations, as well as with the private sector, and manages rural electrification initiatives. The ministry became a separate entity on July 2, 1992, during the P. V. Narasimha Rao government, following the split of the earlier Ministry of Power, Coal and Non-Conventional Energy Sources, which was divided into the Ministry of Power, the Ministry of Coal, and the Ministry of Non-Conventional Energy Sources, later renamed the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy in 2006. The current Union Cabinet Minister is Manohar Lal Khattar. In 2012, the ministry inaugurated the Smart Grid project in Puducherry. The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission is also associated with the ministry.
